# Neostella API (1.0.0)

# [link  to section/Introduction](https://api.neostella.app/docs/\#section/Introduction) Introduction

👋 Welcome to the **Neostella API**, where we're all about making your legal life easier.

* * *

## [link  to section/introduction/Authentication](https://api.neostella.app/docs/\#section/introduction/Authentication) Authentication

All API endpoints require authentication using a **Bearer Token**. To access any resource, include the token in the `Authorization` header of your request in the following format: `Authorization: Bearer <TOKEN>`. Requests that do not include a valid bearer token will be rejected with a 401 Unauthorized error. Make sure to keep your token secure, as it grants full access to the API on your behalf.

* * *

## [link  to section/introduction/Authorization](https://api.neostella.app/docs/\#section/introduction/Authorization) Authorization

In addition to requiring a valid bearer token, all API endpoints enforce **scope-based authorization**. Each endpoint requires the token to include a specific scope that grants permission to access that resource. If the provided token does not contain the necessary scope, the request will be denied with a 403 Forbidden error. Ensure that the token you use has the correct scopes assigned for the operations you intend to perform.

* * *

## [link  to section/introduction/Special-field-types](https://api.neostella.app/docs/\#section/introduction/Special-field-types) Special field types

Most fields on a record hold a simple value (text, number, date, choice). Five field types are **special**: their values are structured objects that the platform stores and manages centrally so they can be validated, searched, and reused consistently everywhere they appear.

##### [link  to section/introduction/Phone](https://api.neostella.app/docs/\#section/introduction/Phone) Phone

A phone number. Properties: `phone_number` (text, required, must be a valid phone number), `phone_type` (text), `ext` (text, up to 5 characters).

##### [link  to section/introduction/Email](https://api.neostella.app/docs/\#section/introduction/Email) Email

An email address. Properties: `email` (text, required), `email_type` (text).

##### [link  to section/introduction/Address](https://api.neostella.app/docs/\#section/introduction/Address) Address

A postal address. All properties are optional. Properties: `street_address` (text), `street_address_line_2` (text), `city` (text), `state` (text), `zip_code` (text), `county` (text), `country` (text), `address_type` (text or the id of a configured address type).

##### [link  to section/introduction/Deadline](https://api.neostella.app/docs/\#section/introduction/Deadline) Deadline

A tracked due date. Properties: `due_date` (date, `YYYY-MM-DD`), `deadline_date` (date, `YYYY-MM-DD`), `deadline_is_met` (boolean).

##### [link  to section/introduction/Period](https://api.neostella.app/docs/\#section/introduction/Period) Period

A date range. Properties: `start_date` (date, `YYYY-MM-DD`), `end_date` (date, `YYYY-MM-DD`).

Any object (persons, organizations, projects, leads, etc) can have fields of these types, they are configured in the schema on the Control Center workspace, and each field is identified by its **selector**.

### [link  to section/introduction/Sending-special-field-values](https://api.neostella.app/docs/\#section/introduction/Sending-special-field-values) Sending special field values

In create and update requests, special fields are set **exactly like any other field**, keyed by the field's selector inside the record's fields. The value is an **object** with the properties listed above, or an **array of objects** when the field is configured as multi-value:

```
{
  "fields": {
    "first_name": "…",
    "phones": [\
      {\
        "phone_number": "+13104209410",\
        "phone_type": "Sales Line",\
        "ext": "123",\
        "system_type": ["primary"]\
      },\
      {\
        "phone_number": "+14145550100",\
        "phone_type": "Mobile"\
      }\
    ],
    "emails": [\
      {\
        "email": "billing@example.com",\
        "email_type": "Work",\
        "system_type": ["primary"]\
      },\
      {\
        "email": "personal@example.com",\
        "email_type": "General"\
      }\
    ],
    "addresses": [\
      {\
        "address_type": "Work",\
        "street_address": "325 E Chicago St",\
        "city": "Milwaukee",\
        "state": "WI",\
        "zip_code": "53202",\
        "country": "USA",\
        "system_type": ["primary"]\
      }\
    ],
    "statute_of_limitations_due_date": {
      "deadline_date": "2027-03-01",
      "deadline_is_met": false
    }
  }
}
```

Rules to keep in mind:

- **Contact phones, emails, and addresses are lists.** A contact holds all of its phone numbers under `phones`, all of its email addresses under `emails`, and all of its addresses under `addresses` — there are no separate primary fields.
- **The primary entry is flagged with `system_type`**: include `"system_type": ["primary"]` on the entry that should be treated as the record's primary phone/email/address. Entries without it are additional values.
- **Single vs. multi-value** is defined by the field's configuration on the schema (`is_list`). Sending a single object to a multi-value field is accepted (it is treated as a one-element list); sending multiple values to a single-value field is not.
- **Partial objects are fine** — all address properties are optional, for example. Provide what you have.
- **Email addresses are normalized**: leading/trailing whitespace is removed and the address is lowercased on save. Expect the normalized form in responses.
- **Updating a value means replacing it**: send the field's new complete list (or object). There is no property-level patching inside a special field value.

### [link  to section/introduction/Reading-special-field-values](https://api.neostella.app/docs/\#section/introduction/Reading-special-field-values) Reading special field values

In responses, special fields come back under the same field selector, with the **same property names used in requests**, as arrays for list fields. The primary entry carries `system_type: ["primary"]`:

```
"phones": [\
  {\
    "phone_number": "+13104209410",\
    "phone_type": "Sales Line",\
    "ext": "123",\
    "system_type": ["primary"]\
  }\
],
"emails": [\
  {\
    "email": "carlos.lopez@example.com",\
    "email_type": "General",\
    "system_type": ["primary"]\
  }\
]
```

### [link  to section/introduction/Notes](https://api.neostella.app/docs/\#section/introduction/Notes) Notes

- Identical values are **deduplicated platform-wide**: if two contacts share a phone number, the platform stores that number once and links it to both. This has no visible effect on the API contract, but explains why value objects carry their own identifiers.
- Access to special field values follows the **permissions of the record they belong to** — there are no separate permissions on the values themselves. Individual fields may additionally be restricted by field-level permissions, in which case their values are omitted from responses for users without access.
